newsitem.title: USA: Taped brutality prompts move of Texas prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Taped brutality prompts move of Texas prisoners.

text.p: Missouri officials on Tuesday were considering legal action against the operators of a Texas jail where guards videotaped prisoners being brutalized.

A spokesman for Gov. Mel Carhahan said the state was reviewing all of its contracts with Texas jails where hundreds of prisoners have been housed under rent-a-cell contracts designed to ease overcrowding in the Missouri prison system.

Chris Sifford, Carnahan's press secretary, said "we are also considering legal action" against the operators of the Brazoria County jail south of Houston to seek reimbursement of money already spent under a now-cancelled $6 million contract.

The Missouri Department of Corrections said temporary facilities were being put together in prison gymnasiums and other facilities to house the prisoners being brought back to the state from the Brazoria jail.
As of Tuesday 200 Missouri convicts had been returned and another 215 were to be brought back in a few days. About 700 other Missouri prisoners were housed in several other Texas institutions.

The action was prompted by release of a tape showing guards at the jail rousting inmates during a drug raid nearly one year ago. The tape showed prisoners being forced to crawl. One was was attacked by a dog and another with an injured ankle was shot in the buttocks with a stun gun.

Officials at the Texas jail said the guards there made the tape as a "training film" to demonstrate "what not to do" to quell a prison uprising, adding that the allegations of abuse had been blown out of proportion.
Missouri had been paying the contractor operating the Texas jail about $17,000 a day to house the Missouri prisoners. The state has since cancelled the contract.

It was not immediately clear if the case would have any impact on other jail rental contracts in Texas where an oversupply of jail space has caused several states to ship about 5,000 prisoners into the Lone Star State.

The tape had not been made public but was aired at a closed county government meeting held to discuss a $100,000 suit filed against the county sheriff by one of the Missouri inmates who said he was among those abused in the incident.
A local newspaper later obtained the tape.
Missouri had been sending prisoners to Texas because of severe overcrowding, pending the construction of additional jail space.

"We are in the process of reviewing all of our contracts in Texas," Sifford said. "We will send a team down there. It is something we would have done in the normal course of business but it will now be stepped up."
